headline: Iran warns: without Washington's compliance, the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen
summary: Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Tehran agreed with Oman on transit conditions for the strait. He said it will not reopen without Washington's compliance.
why: The Strait of Hormuz is a major oil transit route, so its status directly affects global crude supply and shipping costs.
why_moved: A stated closure of the strait pending US compliance keeps Gulf crude supply uncertain, supporting oil prices.
